ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All direct and indirect owners, general partners, limited partners at or above the 25 percent UBO threshold, and authorized signatories of the Hong Kong investor must be screened against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, HKSAR targeted financial sanctions under the United Nations Sanctions Ordinance (Cap. 537), and China's Unreliable Entity List and national security-related sanctions. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person, including domestic PEPs, international PEPs, their family members, and close associates; senior management approval, documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis, and ongoing transaction monitoring at least every 90 days are required. All screening results, negative-news searches, and UBO verification records must be retained for at least five years and made available to the SAMR, PBOC, and other competent authorities upon lawful request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Declaration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), supplemented by the provincial-level SAMR online registration portal; for the Hong Kong investor, the Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Registration and Information System (IRIS) name search is used as a supplementary cross-border check.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Foreign-Invested Partnership name must be registered in Simplified Chinese characters using the four-tier naming sequence: administrative division, distinctive name, industry or business characteristic, and organization form. The organization form must be '合伙企业' or '有限合伙企业', and any token implying a corporate form such as Limited, Ltd., Corporation, or Inc. is prohibited. An English commercial name may be used as a phonetic transliteration or trade dress, but it is not the statutory registration name; the SAMR record remains the Chinese name. Pinyin transliteration of a foreign partner's name is allowed if it is phonetically faithful and does not create confusion with prohibited or sensitive tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name declaration is rejected, the applicant receives a written rejection notice citing the statutory basis. Within 60 days of receipt, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the next higher market-regulation authority under the PRC Administrative Reconsideration Law. The applicant should also request a short extension of the name-reservation filing window if a similar conflicting name has been released or cancelled. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant must obtain the relevant ministerial approval letter and re-file. If the rejection is based on similarity to a previously registered name, the applicant may either obtain the existing holder's written consent or challenge the prior registration administratively. A court appeal may be commenced within six months after the reconsideration decision or the authority's failure to reply. All filings, time-stamped declarations, and rejection notices should be preserved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership in the remote desktop access and unattended machine telemetry software industry, a pure virtual office, registered-agent mailbox, or commercial drop address is not permissible. The SAMR, the local tax bureau, and the bank opening the FIP's RMB and foreign-currency accounts all expect a physical place of business in Mainland China. A serviced office or co-working space with a dedicated desk, a valid lease, ongoing utility bills, and actual staff presence is acceptable. A mailbox-only premise or an address used solely as a registered office will be rejected for tax registration and bank account opening, and will trigger administrative penalties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection by SAMR or municipal tax authorities: valid lease agreement covering the registered office; utility bill or property management fee invoice in the FIP name; visible business license and Chinese nameplate; actual servers, workstations, networking equipment, and software-development records consistent with the IoT telemetry and remote screen-share business; at least one responsible person or employee available during working hours; payroll and social-insurance records for any staff; accounting ledgers, invoices, and books kept at the office or at a locatable professional address; and no mismatch between the registered office and the actual operational address. Quantified risk: for a low-risk technology FIP with a genuine serviced-office lease, the probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months is approximately 15 to 25 percent; if a virtual office or mailbox address is used, the risk is 100 percent non-compliance and a physical inspection should be assumed imminent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China (2006 Revision, amended 2014), Articles 2, 8, 14, 16, 19 and 62; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 3, 26 and 31; Administrative Measures for the Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprises (2010), Articles 4, 7, 10 and 16; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, effective 1 March 2022), Articles 2, 15, 20 and 27; and Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures (Ministry of Commerce Decree No. 2 of 2020), Articles 5, 8 and 12.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) acting through the Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise Registration Desk of the local Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSAB) where the registered office is located, with integrated foreign investment information reporting to the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and exchange-control reporting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form combined with the Foreign Investment Information Report and the executed Partnership Agreement; where applicable, the Name Pre-Approval Certificate issued by the SAMR national name registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The People's Republic of China imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital or mandated blocked escrow account for a foreign-invested limited partnership. The capital amounts subscribed by each partner, the form of contribution (cash, in-kind, intellectual property, equipment, or other lawful property), and the contribution schedule are fixed contractually in the Partnership Agreement. Inbound capital from the Hong Kong SAR investor must be reported under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures and registered with SAFE through a designated bank before remittance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF PARTNERS RESOLUTION OF [●] FOREIGN-INVESTED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (THE PARTNERSHIP) ADOPTED BY THE UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF ALL PARTNERS ON [●]. WHEREAS, the Partners have agreed to form a foreign-invested limited partnership under the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of computer programming, remote desktop access software, unattended machine telemetry, internet-of-things support services, and related software publishing activities; and WHEREAS, the Partnership Agreement dated [●] sets forth the capital contributions, profit allocation, management structure, and governance rules; and WHEREAS, the Partnership has selected a registered office located at [●], [City], People's Republic of China; and WHEREAS, it is necessary to authorize the opening of bank accounts and to appoint statutory officers to carry out the formation and operational requirements of the Partnership; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, subject to the Partnership Agreement and applicable law, as follows: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION: The capital subscriptions of each partner as set forth in Contribution Schedule A are approved, ratified, and confirmed. Such subscriptions constitute partnership capital and not share capital. The Managing Partner is expressly authorized and directed to demand, receive, receipt, and deposit all subscribed capital into the Partnership's bank account on or before the contribution deadlines stated in the Partnership Agreement. No escrow account is required by law, but all capital receipts shall be recorded in the partnership contribution ledger and reported in the foreign investment information report. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office located at [●], [City], People's Republic of China is hereby adopted as the Partnership's statutory registered address and principal place of administration. The Managing Partner is authorized to execute the lease, accept service of process, and make all necessary filings with the local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Partners authorize the opening of one RMB basic deposit account and one foreign-currency capital account at [●] Bank or another SAFE-designated bank. The Managing Partner and the Compliance Officer shall act as joint authorized signatories for amounts above [●] and as individual signatories for routine administrative payments. The Managing Partner is authorized to execute bank mandate forms, beneficiary declarations, source-of-funds statements, and onboarding documentation for Stripe, Paddle, and related payment rails. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [●] is appointed as Managing Partner and statutory representative of the Partnership; [●] is appointed as Partnership Compliance Officer; and [●] is appointed as Finance Controller. Each appointee is vested with full authority to sign government filings, tax declarations, social insurance registrations, foreign exchange filings, and partnership records, and to represent the Partnership before SAMR, MOFCOM, SAFE, the tax authorities, banks, and commercial counterparties. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION AND RATIFICATION: The Managing Partner is authorized to execute all documents, appoint legal and notarial agents, communicate with the Hong Kong SAR investor, and take every lawful step necessary to complete the formation and governance of the Partnership. Any act performed by the Managing Partner, Compliance Officer, or Finance Controller in the name of the Partnership before the date and time of this Resolution is hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved in all respects. This Resolution shall remain in full force and effect until revoked by a subsequent written resolution of the Partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Preliminary Foreign Investment Information Assembly
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration System and the local Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the establishment application, all partners must execute a notarized power of attorney in favor of the authorized representative or registered agency. The proposed partnership name must be submitted to the SAMR name-registration module and must follow the required pattern of administrative division, distinctive trade name, principal business descriptor, and the legal suffix 'Foreign-Invested Partnership (Limited Partnership)' or a substantially equivalent suffix accepted by the local MSAB. Simultaneously, the partners must prepare the preliminary Foreign Investment Information Report data, including the Hong Kong SAR investor's ultimate beneficial owner details, proposed capital contribution schedule, business scope, and registered office address. The name review authority will check for conflicts, prohibited words, and misleading elements. Once the name pre-approval certificate is issued, its unique approval code must be preserved and referenced in the establishment application. If any foreign partner is a legal person, its certificate of incorporation and good standing status certificate must be apostilled in the place of issue under the Hague Apostille Convention and, where required, translated into Chinese by a qualified translation agency for attachment to the later registration package.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney executed by each partner or by the authorized agent
Draft Partnership Agreement signed by all partners
Name pre-approval application and, after issuance, the certificate of name pre-approval
Certified passport or identity document copies of all individual partners
Certificate of incorporation and good standing certificate of the Hong Kong SAR investing partner, apostilled or legalized as applicable
Ultimate beneficial owner statement and source-of-funds declaration
Initial contribution schedule and proposed business scope
Registered office letter of intent or lease proposal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is rejected or placed in suspense for similarity, the applicant shall file objections or submit three alternate names within five working days. If the rejection is based on restricted words, the applicant must remove the offending words or obtain the relevant authorization letter from the competent authority. Any deficiency in the legalization of foreign partner documents must be cured by obtaining a replacement apostille or notarial copy before the establishment filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Foreign-Invested Partnership Establishment Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSAB) Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise Registration Desk, with integrated reporting to the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorized representative or agent must lodgethe complete establishment application package with the Foreign-Invested Partnership Registration Desk of the MSAB in whose district the registered office is located, or through the authenticated SAMR online portal. The signed application form must be accompanied by the original Partnership Agreement, the name pre-approval certificate, apostilled identity documents of every foreign partner, and the registered office proof. The MSAB examiner will verify that the business scope is consistent with the negative list for foreign investment access, that the partnership form is permissible, and that the proposed name and registered address are lawful. If the application passes examination, the MSAB issues the Foreign-Invested Partnership business license and automatically transmits the foreign investment information report to MOFCOM under the integrated one-window service. The applicant must review the business license data against the Partnership Agreement before leaving the registry window. Where the Hong Kong SAR investor is a limited partner, the certificate of compliance must expressly identify the nature and extent of that partner's interest and any restriction on management participation.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form, signed or notarized as required
Original executed Partnership Agreement
Certificate of name pre-approval
Apostilled or legalized identity and existence documents of all partners
Registered office lease agreement and landlord title certificate
Power of attorney and identity of the authorized representative
Foreign Investment Information Report form
Partners' resolution approving the formation and capital structure
Execution pages of the Partnership Agreement bearing signatures or seals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MSAB issues a query or deficiency notice, the applicant must cure all deficiencies within fifteen working days from the date of notice. If the application is suspended because of a negative-list concern, the partnership must amend its business scope or remove the prohibited activity and resubmit. If the foreign investment information report is rejected for incomplete beneficial ownership data, the applicant must remediate the report and may appeal to the next higher-level MSAB if the examiner refuses to accept a corrected submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Foreign Exchange, and Statutory Information Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local service bureau; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through designated banks; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; MOFCOM integrated reporting platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, the partnership must complete mandatory post-establishment administrative formalities without delay. The national market registry data push generally creates the partnership's taxpayer file automatically, but the partnership must still supply supplementary information to the local tax bureau through the e-tax platform, including accounting standards, responsible person, payroll method, invoice quota, and tax-filing calendar. For inbound contributions from the Hong Kong SAR partner, the partnership must perform the SAFE foreign direct investment (FDI) registration at a SAFE-designated bank, submitting the business license, partnership agreement, contribution schedule, and FDI basic information form to obtain a capital account facility. The partnership must also file the formal foreign investment information report with MOFCOM through the integrated platform, and, if employees are hired, register for social insurance and housing fund at the local HRSS bureau. Any delay in SAFE registration may prevent inward capital remittances; therefore the managing partner should complete this step before invoicing or receiving foreign software subscription revenue.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Partnership business license (original and copy)
Executed Partnership Agreement and capital contribution schedule
SAFE foreign direct investment basic information form
Tax registration supplementary information form
Managing Partner and Compliance Officer identification documents
Registered office lease and business license address proof
Foreign partner bank details and shareholder structure chart
Foreign Investment Information Report confirmation receipt
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is not automatically completed or the taxpayer identity is inconsistent with the business license, the fiscal representative must appear at the local tax service hall with the business license and partnership agreement to apply for manual registration rectification. If SAFE rejects the FDI application for data mismatch, the partnership must correct the beneficial ownership and contribution schedule in the Partnership Agreement and resubmit with a cover letter explaining the discrepancy before any inbound capital remittance is attempted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution Injection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAFE-designated commercial bank and People's Bank of China (PBOC) account filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Finance Controller shall open a RMB basic deposit account at a commercial bank within the municipality where the partnership is registered, and a foreign-currency capital account at a SAFE-designated bank if the Hong Kong SAR partner will inject capital. The bank will conduct customer due diligence, verify the business license, confirm the identity of authorized signatories, and review the Partners' Resolution authorizing the account mandate. The Managing Partner and Compliance Officer must attend in person or appear through a notarized representative to execute account opening forms, specimen signature cards, and KYC declarations. After the accounts are opened, the initial capital contribution must be injected in accordance with the contribution schedule. Inward remittances from the Hong Kong SAR partner must be credited to the capital account and recorded as foreign direct investment under SAFE rules. The bank will issue capital inflow receipts and a confirmation of deposit, which the Finance Controller must maintain in the partnership ledger. The partnership may then complete Stripe and Paddle payment-rail onboarding using the business license, bank identification documents, and bank statements; no separate payment institution license is required for the partnership as the commercial model is remote software sales.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Partnership business license
Official company seal and financial seal, if used by the partnership
Partners' Resolution authorizing account opening and signatories
Managing Partner and Compliance Officer passports or identity cards
Executed Partnership Agreement and contribution schedule
SAFE FDI registration confirmation or bank transaction code
Beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds statement
Bank account mandate forms and specimen signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application due to insufficient KYC information, the partnership must provide a more detailed source-of-funds narrative, audited financial statements or bank reference letters from the Hong Kong SAR investor, and a revised ownership diagram. If the SAFE capital account facility is denied, the partnership should approach an alternative SAFE-designated bank, and if the issue persists, seek guidance from the local SAFE branch to obtain a written rectification notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formation Completion, Registered Records, and Ongoing Annual Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS); MOFCOM integrated foreign investment reporting platform; local tax authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days of incorporation, the Compliance Officer must assemble a formation completion binder containing the business license, Partnership Agreement, contribution schedule, bank account evidence, tax registration confirmation, SAFE FDI registration, and the foreign investment information report receipt. The binder shall be held at the registered office and made available to tax, audit, or regulatory inspectors upon request. The partnership must maintain an accurate register of partners, capital contributions, profit distributions, and ultimate beneficial owners. Annually, between April 1 and June 30, the partnership must submit the foreign investment information annual report and the market entity annual report through NECIPS, including any changes in partners, capital, ownership, business scope, or registered address. Because the partnership's activity is ISIC 6201 software programming and remote desktop/telemetry software sales, no industrial operating license, Environmental Impact Assessment, or Civil Defense fire permit is triggered. If the partnership operates a public website on servers located in China, it must complete the applicable ICP filing under the Internet Information Service Administrative Measures; this is a filing, not an industrial license, and does not alter the non-manufacturing classification.
required_dossiers: Formation completion binder or registered statutory records
Annual Foreign Investment Information Report data
Annual financial statements and capital contribution ledger
Notice of changes to partners, capital, or business scope, if any
NECIPS login credentials and filing confirmation
Government correspondence and license register
Office lease and insurance records
Software licensing and sales contracts for commercial records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual report is flagged by SAMR for inconsistency or late filing, the partnership must submit a corrected annual report through NECIPS within ten working days to avoid being placed on the list of enterprises with abnormal operations. If MOFCOM notifies the partnership of data gaps in the foreign investment information report, the Compliance Officer must respond within the time limit stated in the notice and provide an amendment with supporting partnership resolutions and updated beneficial ownership information.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable (no municipal industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over a pure software entity under ISIC 6201; the entity conducts no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing activity).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable (no industrial operating license is required for remote desktop access software, unattended machine telemetry, or IoT support software under the reference statutory classification; no manufacturing permit, chemical facility permit, or warehouse license is triggered).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable (no Environmental Impact Assessment agency jurisdiction because the activity is purely digital and does not involve a regulated physical project).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable (no EIA tier applies; no full EIA report, environmental registration, or exemption certificate is required for a software development and remote services entity).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable (zero industrial discharge; the entity generates no industrial wastewater, volatile organic compounds, hazardous waste, or process emissions from manufacturing operations; only ordinary office waste streams may apply under municipal waste management rules).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial civil-defense fire permits because the partnership engages in no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. If a commercial office occupies premises, the office must comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, maintain ordinary fire safety inspection records, and satisfy standard workplace safety and occupational health requirements; no Civil Defense fire permit is required for pure software operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, with filings made through the STA Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) platform; for the Hong Kong SAR element, the separate competent authority is the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) through the IRD e-Tax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a China-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP): first, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues the Foreign-Invested Partnership Business License and the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which automatically becomes the PRC tax identification number; second, the FIP is required to activate tax registration in the STA e-Tax platform and ensure the registered scope covers remote screen-share/IoT telemetry software services; third, a foreign non-resident partner that has no fixed place of business in China must either obtain a non-resident tax identification number from the competent STA office or be subject to withholding filing by the partnership; the documentary package includes the foreign partner's certificate of incorporation, tax/residence certificate, notarized power of attorney if applicable, the partnership agreement, SAMR business license, and beneficial owner proof supporting any tax treaty claim. For the HK jurisdiction node, the FIP should apply to the IRD under the Business Registration Ordinance for a Business Registration Certificate and may be required to file Profits Tax returns only if it has Hong Kong-sourced profits; the Hong Kong Business Registration Number is the documentary identity used on invoices issued from that node.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under PRC law: China does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. The FIP is statutorily fiscally transparent; the partnership does not pay enterprise income tax, and each partner reports distributive share. Partnership allocations are respected only where they have substantial economic effect and genuinely reflect the partners' economic risk. Hybrid mismatch and anti-abuse rules may recharacterise cross-border payments or disallow double-dip outcomes. No entity-level C-corporation type election is available to a partnership.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under PRC VAT law; remote desktop access and unattended IoT telemetry software are treated as modern services subject to the 6% domestic VAT rate unless exported. Hong Kong SAR itself imposes no VAT, GST, or general sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (annual taxable sales) is the mandatory threshold for registration as a general VAT taxpayer; below that threshold the FIP may remain a small-scale taxpayer with simplified levy, but VAT registration and the collection of Special Value-Added Tax Invoices are required once the threshold is exceeded or if voluntary registration is desirable for input VAT credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Golden Tax IV system requires all VAT invoices, including Fully Digitalised Electronic Invoices (FDED), to be issued through the STA electronic invoicing platform. Invoice data must be transmitted to the tax authority in near-real-time, each invoice receives a unique tax-control number and digital stamp, and no offline or unauthorised local invoice can be used. B2B sales require Special Value-Added Tax Invoices to allow the buyer's input VAT credit, and each special invoice must be cleared and matched through the national e-invoice database.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The FIP may claim zero-rating for qualifying exports of remote screen-share and IoT telemetry software services where the service is supplied to an overseas customer, the service is consumed entirely outside mainland China, the software is delivered purely by electronic download or cloud access, and consideration is paid in foreign currency and repatriated through a licensed bank. Pure software downloads do not require a customs declaration, but physical IoT hardware or software carriers leaving China qualify for the goods export zero-rate only with a valid customs export declaration; input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is refundable, whereas VAT on exempt cross-border services would not be refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for physical exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical exports
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued inward remittance receipt
Chinese export VAT invoice (zero-rated export invoice)
State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) export collection record
Software delivery report, server log, IP address evidence, or remote session log for digital services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export zero-rating is not supported at audit, the tax authority will restore output VAT at the applicable domestic rate (6% for services or 13% for goods) and impose late-payment interest at 0.05% per day. A false or fraudulent substantiation package may result in administrative fines equal to 50% to 500% of the tax underpayment, denial and clawback of any input VAT refund, and criminal liability for false VAT invoices or export tax refund fraud under the Criminal Law, including custodial penalties in serious cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and its subordinate State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating RMB regime with current-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. The Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) may freely settle export/service proceeds, pay genuine trade-related expenses, and remit after-tax profits through the designated onshore account; prior approval is not required for such current-account transactions, but SAFE-licensed banks must verify authenticity on the basis of contracts, invoices, customs/VAT declarations and remittance applications. In contrast, capital-account convertibility is still controlled. Foreign partner capital contributions, equity transfers, intragroup loans and foreign-investment liquidation remittances require FDI foreign-exchange registration, capital account opening and post-registration; RMB settlement of foreign-invested partnership capital must be within the scope of the registration and may not be used for prohibited investments such as domestic equity lending. Profit remittance from the FIP is permitted after annual audit and Chinese tax clearance, and the bank will check the residence certificate, tax settlement certificate and payment order. Because Hong Kong is a separate SAR, cross-border flows between the HK parent and the mainland FIP are subject to the same SAFE filing requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: SAFE does not impose a fixed mandatory conversion ratio. The statutory rule is that export/service proceeds must be repatriated to onshore China and credited to the FIP's designated foreign exchange settlement account as soon as the exporting entity receives them, and in no event later than the contractual settlement maturity date; overdue receivables must be reported to the bank with a commercial justification. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent - the FIP may retain 100% of foreign currency in its settlement account or voluntarily convert to RMB at the prevailing market rate. For remote software/IoT services, export proceeds are not supported by export customs declarations; the bank instead requires the executed master subscription agreement, invoices, evidence of service delivery, and the SAFE service trade payment code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic RMB Deposit Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
SAFE-designated Foreign Exchange Capital Account and Operational RMB Current Account
Capital Project Settlement Account and Import/Export Receivables Account
Partnership Basic Deposit Account and RMB/Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under PBoC and SAFE rules, foreign fintech EMIs such as Stripe and Paddle are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in mainland China and cannot legally open or maintain settlement accounts for a Chinese FIP. They may be used only as overseas payment aggregators or billing front-ends; the FIP must repatriate collections through a licensed domestic acquiring bank and/or Tier-1 bank. Any arrangement where a foreign EMI holds the FIP's operating capital or settles its revenue through a commingled wallet would create severe unlicensed payment business and AML risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. The general partner, or the foreign investor appointed as the authorized executive, must attend the bank's KYC interview in person at the branch; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by PBoC-regulated banks for RMB basic deposit accounts. A notarized and China-legalized power of attorney can permit a China-based finance officer to manage account operations, but the general partner's identity verification and face-to-face interview remain non-delegable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell/conduit concern from the HK partner structure with mainland operational substance; bank may look through the FIP to undisclosed natural persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized HK Business Registration and Certificate of Incorporation; CRS and FATCA self-certifications for every partner; PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership business license; foreign investment information filing; beneficial ownership table; mainland office lease and utility invoices; payroll and social insurance records; general partner resolution appointing the authorized account signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated monthly payouts from Stripe/Paddle create third-party payment ambiguity and the appearance of unlicensed FX settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of Stripe/Paddle payout ledgers and settlement reports; customer order IDs and invoices; remote desktop/IoT telemetry session logs; server hosting bills; annual audited financial statements; SAFE service trade contract registration; a three-way reconciliation matching each aggregate payout to subscription identifiers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote screen-share and unattended IoT access is treated as sensitive cyber capability, triggering export-control and cybersecurity enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technical product write-up and data-flow diagram demonstrating lawful remote support; end-user certificates and end-use guarantees; export control classification memo covering ECCN/NTA and China dual-use catalogue; cybersecurity filing evidence; PIPL data protection impact assessment; reseller customer due diligence files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound management fees, royalties, or software licensing payments to the HK partner may be re-characterized as disguised capital repatriation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered intragroup software licensing/SaaS agreement; royalty benchmarking workpaper; withholding tax certificates for VAT and enterprise income tax; service acceptance records and support tickets; SAFE current-account remittance application stamped by the onshore bank; audited capital account and profit distribution resolution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial capital contributions from the HK partner must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 to the FIP's onshore foreign exchange capital account at a SAFE-authorized Tier-1 bank. The remittance narrative must identify the FIP and contain the SAFE FDI registration code issued by the receiving bank. The receiving bank verifies the foreign-investment registration, applies the correct SAFE transaction code for foreign-invested enterprise capital contribution, and upon clearing performs RMB settlement subject to the capital-account use restrictions and the foreign investment negative list. The FIP must then obtain a capital verification report from a licensed Chinese CPA and retain the SAFE capital account registration form; the injected funds cannot be used for prohibited transactions such as RMB lending to domestic parties or speculative investments outside the registered business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade and operating disbursements, the FIP uses SWIFT MT103 wire transfers through its Tier-1 bank after submitting a current-account remittance application, invoice, underlying contract, tax withholding certificate, and where applicable proof of service delivery. Larger software/hardware procurement can be settled through an irrevocable at-sight commercial letter of credit or documentary collections, with the supplier presenting compliant documents against a bank trade desk. Cross-border RMB disbursements should be routed through CIPS using MT103 in CNY where the counterparty supports it; all outgoing payments remain subject to AML sanctions screening and SAFE trade verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB forward contracts for hedges of real current-account receipts and disbursements
Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the Hong Kong parent treasury, not the mainland FIP
RMB/HKD or RMB/USD FX swaps for working capital rebalancing and mismatch management
European-style FX options purchased from an authorized onshore bank, with premium and notional limited to documented transactional exposure
Cross-currency swaps limited to long-term documented current/capital exposures and executed only after SAFE and onshore bank viability review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after expiry of the current certificate, which occurs every 12 months on the anniversary of initial registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a penalty of HKD 300 for up to 3 months; HKD 600 for 3-6 months; HKD 900 for 6-12 months; and HKD 1,200 for over 12 months. Continued operation without a valid certificate is an offence under Section 12 of the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310), punishable by a fine of HKD 5,000 and imprisonment for 1 year. The IRD may also strike the business name from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnerships (Form BIR52) with Financial Statements and Tax Computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued on the first working day of April each year (for fiscal years ending 31 December). Due within 1 month of issue; if a tax representative is appointed, automatic extension to 15 August is available. For non-31 December year-ends, the due date is as stated on the return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is an offence under Section 80(1) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap 112) with a maximum fine of HKD 10,000. The IRD may issue an estimated assessment under Section 59(3) which may be raised by up to 50% as a penalty. For intentional understatement, additional penalties up to HKD 10,000 plus double the undercharged tax may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form BIR56A and BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 1 month of the issue date, normally issued in April each year for the fiscal year ended 31 March. A nil return is required if no employees were employed during the year, unless an exemption has been granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under IRO for failure to file is up to HKD 10,000. If IRD has reason to believe income has been understated, a penalty of up to HKD 10,000 plus double the tax undercharged may be imposed, and in serious cases prosecution with a fine of up to HKD 50,000 and imprisonment for 3 years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Hong Kong law, partnerships are not required to have a statutory audit unless: (1) the partnership is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund (LPF) under the Limited Partnership Funds Ordinance (Cap 637), in which case an annual audit by a licensed CPA (practising) is mandatory; (2) the partnership conducts regulated activities under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap 571) where the Hong Kong Monetary Authority or Securities and Futures Commission requires audited accounts; (3) the Inland Revenue Department issues a notice under Section 51C of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap 112) requiring submission of audited financial statements if annual gross turnover exceeds HKD 5,000,000 or where the IRD believes the accounts are insufficient for tax assessment. Additionally, financial institutions or DNFBPs under the AMLO must have their anti-money laundering systems audited annually. As prudent practice, any partnership with annual turnover exceeding HKD 5,000,000 or total assets exceeding HKD 10,000,000 should engage an independent certified public accountant to perform an audit, especially when dealing with cross-border operations or bank financing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) or HKFRS for Private Entities. If the entity is an LPF that is also a financial institution, full HKFRS or IFRS may be required. The accounting records must be kept in English or Chinese.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose a specific annual UBO confirmation filing for partnerships. However, under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37), any change in the composition of partners, the nature of contributions, or profit-sharing ratios must be reported to the Companies Registry within 30 days of the change. For taxation, the annual Profit Tax Return (BIR52) must be accompanied by a partnership schedule disclosing each partner's share of profit/loss, and the IRD must be notified of any partner changes. If the partnership is registered as an LPF under Cap 637, it must maintain a register of general and limited partners and file an annual return with the Companies Registry. Any changes to the registered details (including UBO information) must be filed within 30 days. Additionally, under the AMLO, if the partnership is a supervised entity, it must conduct ongoing due diligence on its beneficial owners, but no annual filing to a public authority is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (statutory for LPF under Cap 637; recommended for other partnerships)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (statutory for LPF and recommended for all partnerships with secured debts)
Copies of Business Registration Certificate and Partnership Agreement

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 380 - USD 1,280 per annum for registered address, corporate secretarial support, and local agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 - USD 6,500 per annum for a certified audit of a low-risk software/remote support partnership with moderate transaction volume; higher if cross-border structuring or complex tax computations are involved.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Hong Kong Profits Tax: 8.25% on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits and 16.5% on the excess for a qualifying entity under the two-tiered rates regime. The 8.25% rate is generally unavailable where the entity is connected with another entity claiming the two-tiered rates or where an election is not properly made. Hong Kong does not impose a separate corporate income tax, value-added tax, capital gains tax, dividend withholding tax, or general interest withholding tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong follows a territorial-source principle. Profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong are taxable; offshore profits may be excluded subject to source analysis and, for specified foreign-sourced passive income received in Hong Kong, the Foreign Source Income Exemption regime. Qualifying research and development expenditure may receive enhanced deductions of 100% or 300% for qualifying expenditure, subject to statutory conditions. Qualifying intellectual-property acquisition expenditure may receive deductions under applicable provisions. There is no general tax holiday. The two-tiered rates regime reduces the rate on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited for ordinary Hong Kong profits-tax losses, subject to continuity, anti-avoidance, and business-operation requirements. Losses may generally be carried forward indefinitely; Hong Kong does not apply a general five-year limitation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BIR52 Profits Tax Return for Persons Other Than Corporations, including partnerships, filed through the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department's eTAX service or by paper filing. A foreign-invested partnership carrying on business in Hong Kong should ordinarily use BIR52 rather than the corporate BIR51. BIR51 applies to companies. BIR54 may be relevant where an agent files for a non-resident person.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with provisional profits tax payments made by installments. There is no general quarterly profits-tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The normal statutory deadline is generally one month after the date printed on the profits-tax return. The Inland Revenue Department grants administrative extension schemes, commonly including block extensions for taxpayers represented by tax practitioners, subject to the applicable filing list and conditions. Provisional profits tax is generally payable in two installments, with the balance and final assessment mechanics determined by the assessment notice. An extension for filing does not automatically extend payment deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the partnership's legal name, business registration number, registered or principal business address, accounting period, commencement date, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partnership must disclose its Hong Kong business activities, Hong Kong representative or agent, and any permanent establishment or fixed place of business relevant to Hong Kong source analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Describe the remote-support software, remote desktop access, unattended machine telemetry, IoT monitoring, licensing, subscription, technical support, and related activities actually conducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State where software development, server operations, customer contracting, sales, support, management, and key decision-making occur. Do not describe offshore activities as Hong Kong activities unless supported by facts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting period, turnover, cost of sales, operating expenses, depreciation, finance costs, foreign-exchange items, and net accounting profit or loss, supported by financial statements and tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign branch or offshore profits only where source evidence, operational records, contracts, personnel evidence, and transaction-level analysis support the exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjust accounting profit for non-deductible expenditure, private or capital expenditure, book depreciation, provisions not satisfying statutory requirements, and other tax adjustments; claim permitted deductions and tax depreciation allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income and expenses using a consistent, documented basis. Software development, cloud infrastructure, payment processing, marketing, and support costs require clear nexus to the relevant revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Break down software subscriptions, license fees, implementation fees, support fees, data or telemetry services, advertising, and other receipts by customer location, contracting entity, performance activity, and source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Customer residence alone does not determine Hong Kong source. The effective operations generating the profits and the place where profit-producing activities occur are material.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose relevant related-party transactions, including development services, management fees, royalties, hosting, financing, commissions, cost allocations, and intercompany software or IP arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's-length pricing and retain master-file, local-file, benchmarking, intercompany agreement, and benefits evidence where documentation requirements or materiality thresholds apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim statutory allowances for qualifying plant, machinery, or specified intellectual-property expenditure and distinguish acquired IP from internally developed software and ordinary operating costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify legal ownership, economic ownership, development functions, enhancement functions, protection functions, exploitation functions, and relevant payment flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter current-year adjusted loss, brought-forward loss, utilized loss, and carried-forward loss. Ordinary losses are generally carried forward indefinitely.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain continuity of the trade and evidence against artificial loss trafficking. Changes in ownership, business cessation, or arrangements lacking commercial purpose may restrict utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the basis for provisional profits tax and reconcile prior-year assessment, payments, current-year estimate, and requested reduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A reduction application must be made within the statutory time limit and supported by a reasonable estimate; an understated estimate can result in surcharge or interest consequences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify offshore profits, foreign taxes, foreign tax credits, and any claim under a comprehensive double-taxation arrangement or the foreign-source income exemption regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction source analysis and foreign tax documentation. Receipt in Hong Kong may be relevant under the foreign-source passive-income rules even where the original income is offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The authorized partner, responsible person, or duly authorized agent must certify the return. Attach accounts, tax computation, schedules, and supporting documents where required by the return or the Inland Revenue Department.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing authority must be validly documented. False certification, omitted income, or unsupported offshore claims can expose the entity and responsible individuals to enforcement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file may lead to a penalty of up to HKD 10,000 under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, additional tax of up to three times the tax undercharged, repeated default action, estimated assessment, prosecution, and recovery proceedings. Tax evasion or fraudulent conduct may attract substantially higher criminal sanctions, including fines, treble tax, and imprisonment. Late payment may result in surcharge, commonly up to 5% and, after an additional statutory period, a further surcharge of up to 10% of the amount outstanding.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% Hong Kong withholding tax on dividends paid by a Hong Kong entity. Hong Kong generally does not impose withholding tax on dividends, including dividends paid to non-residents. Partnership profit allocations are not dividends; their treatment depends on the partner's status, source, and applicable foreign tax law.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Hong Kong has a comprehensive double-taxation arrangement with Mainland China. Relief for Mainland-source income or Hong Kong-source income is generally claimed in the jurisdiction imposing the tax by submitting the relevant tax return, treaty-relief form, beneficial-ownership information, transaction documents, and a Hong Kong Certificate of Resident Status where required. A Certificate of Resident Status is issued by the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department only where the applicant satisfies the applicable residence and substance conditions. Treaty entitlement does not override beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, source, permanent-establishment, or principal-purpose limitations. Hong Kong payors normally do not withhold dividend tax, so there is no general Hong Kong refund process for dividend withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong generally imposes 0% withholding tax on outbound interest. Royalties paid to a non-resident may be deemed taxable Hong Kong assessable profits where the statutory conditions are met. The domestic effective rate is generally 4.95% where the royalty is paid to an unrelated non-resident and the relevant IP was not previously owned by a Hong Kong person; it can be 16.5% where the statutory related-party or IP-use conditions produce a full-rate charge. Under the Mainland China-Hong Kong arrangement, the treaty ceiling is generally 7% for royalties and 7% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership, source, residence, anti-abuse, and other treaty conditions. The domestic rate applies where it is lower or where treaty relief is unavailable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Hong Kong local-file and master-file documentation requirements generally apply unless an exemption is available. A Hong Kong entity is generally exempt from preparing a master file and local file if it does not exceed at least two of these three size thresholds: HKD 400,000,000 annual revenue, HKD 300,000,000 total assets, and 100 employees. Separate local-file transaction thresholds generally exempt controlled transactions not exceeding HKD 220,000,000 for transfer of financial assets, HKD 220,000,000 for transfer of intellectual property, HKD 440,000,000 for transfer of goods, or HKD 110,000,000 for other transactions, subject to statutory aggregation and classification rules. Records must generally be retained for at least seven years.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the selected method produces the most reliable arm's-length result
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong has no general standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to the economic-substance legislation of certain offshore jurisdictions. However, substance is material to source-of-profits analysis, beneficial ownership, treaty access, transfer pricing, anti-avoidance, and the Foreign Source Income Exemption regime. For foreign-sourced passive income received in Hong Kong, qualifying entities may need to satisfy economic-substance requirements for interest income or disposal gains, or participation-exemption requirements for dividends and equity disposal gains. Relevant substance generally includes adequate qualified employees and adequate operating expenditure in Hong Kong, proportionate to the activities generating the income. Outsourcing may be accepted only with adequate supervision, control, and records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting software subscription revenue, understating related-party receipts, fabricating expenses, concealing Hong Kong profit-producing activities, or submitting a false offshore-claim narrative.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance may result in a fine of up to HKD 50,000 per offence, a further fine equal to three times the tax undercharged, and imprisonment of up to three years, in addition to assessment, recovery, and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Partners, authorized signatories, agents, and responsible officers may be prosecuted where their own consent, connivance, neglect, or participation is established. Civil recovery and tax assessment may continue against the taxpayer. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax sanction but may arise from separate court or criminal procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file BIR52, failure to make provisional-tax payments, filing after an approved extension has expired, or ignoring estimated assessments and payment demands.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties may include up to HKD 10,000 for filing default, additional tax up to three times the tax undercharged, estimated assessment, payment surcharge, civil recovery, prosecution, and enforcement against assets or bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability is not automatic merely because an individual is a director or partner. It may arise for statutory offences personally committed or where separate guarantees, fraud, misfeasance, or insolvency-law breaches are established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, development fees, cloud-hosting charges, financing margins, or cost allocations to shift profits without functions, assets, risks, comparable evidence, or commercial benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Inland Revenue Department may adjust assessable profits, deny deductions, impose compensating assessments, apply penalties for incorrect returns, and pursue anti-avoidance or tax-evasion proceedings where intentional conduct is present. Documentation failures can independently create compliance exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons can face prosecution for knowingly false information or participation in evasion. Ordinary TP adjustments generally impose entity-level tax rather than automatic personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating or contracting through Hong Kong while personnel, development, sales, customer support, server administration, and strategic decision-making actually occur in Hong Kong or another jurisdiction, followed by unsupported exclusion of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Inland Revenue Department may treat profits as Hong Kong sourced, deny the offshore claim, assess tax and penalties, and apply anti-avoidance principles. Foreign-source passive income received in Hong Kong may also be taxable under the Foreign Source Income Exemption rules unless an exemption condition is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals directing false source records, sham arrangements, or misleading filings may face criminal exposure. Corporate separateness does not protect deliberate fraud or statutory offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing interest, royalties, or other income through a Hong Kong partnership with no operational substance, no control over the relevant IP or financing, and no entitlement to treaty benefits, while misrepresenting the partnership as the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty relief may be denied, domestic withholding or source-country tax may apply, and interest, penalties, assessments, and anti-avoidance consequences may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals responsible for false residence certificates, beneficial-ownership declarations, or sham structures may face civil and criminal consequences in the relevant jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the software business in Hong Kong without a valid Business Registration Certificate, failing to renew it, using an incorrect legal name, or omitting business locations and activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to comply with the Business Registration Ordinance may result in prosecution, fines, and possible imprisonment under the applicable provisions, separate from profits-tax assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible individual or partner may be prosecuted for the default. Corporate or partnership status does not immunize a person from a personal statutory offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing payments through Stripe, Paddle, banks, or payment intermediaries using undisclosed beneficial owners, fictitious merchants, sanctioned counterparties, suspicious refund patterns, or customer funds inconsistent with the declared remote-software business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Applicable obligations may arise under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, United Nations sanctions legislation, payment-services rules, and contractual platform controls. Consequences can include account freezing, transaction rejection, regulatory investigation, fines, and imprisonment for serious offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly facilitate money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions evasion, or false onboarding information may face personal criminal liability, confiscation, restraint orders, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a competent court in related criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the remote-support platform to provide regulated telecommunications, stored-value, payment, money-service, cybersecurity, surveillance, or other licensed services beyond ordinary software licensing and technical support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Operating a regulated activity without the required licence may result in injunctions, business interruption, fines, prosecution, and sector-specific imprisonment provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, partners, and managers who knowingly authorize unlicensed operations may be personally prosecuted and may be subject to disqualification or other regulatory orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using third-party source code, open-source software, telemetry libraries, encryption technology, trademarks, or customer data without valid rights, licence compliance, or export-control review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include injunctions, damages, account of profits, delivery-up or destruction orders, criminal copyright penalties in applicable cases, contract termination, and tax deduction denial for unsupported payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise for knowing infringement, dishonest assistance, fraudulent misrepresentation, or breach of fiduciary duty. Ordinary inadvertent infringement is generally an entity-level civil matter.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Preferentially repatriating funds to related parties, transferring IP or customer contracts below value, incurring taxes while insolvent, or stripping assets before creditor claims are resolved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transactions may be challenged or reversed under insolvency law, with contribution orders, restoration of assets, fines, disqualification, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent trading or misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners may face personal contribution orders, civil restitution, disqualification, and imprisonment where fraudulent or reckless conduct is proven. A separate legal personality does not shield fraudulent asset diversion.
